title: Agent use cases — and when they are overkill

videos.script: Lesson one showed what an agent is. This lesson asks when you should build one, and the honest answer is: less often than the noise suggests. {{title}} An agent earns its cost when the path cannot be written down in advance. Research across sources. A support case that could go five ways. A bug whose cause nobody knows yet. {{earn}} Most tasks are not like that. The path is known, and a workflow does the job cheaper, faster and more predictably. {{workflow}} You will measure that. The same three customer messages, answered by a router that calls the model once, and by lesson one's agent. Count the requests, the tokens and the seconds. {{measure}} Then a piece of arithmetic that every agent designer should do once. If each step is right ninety-five times in a hundred, ten steps in a row are right only sixty times. {{compound}} And one more question, the one that decides how careful you must be. Can the action be undone? {{undo}}
